nodes.label: GET /master/material-assignments (Material Assignment Pagination)
nodes.rationale: Rows carry parent_id, server_groups, group_type (extended_material_group) and group_value, so a material assignment is a hierarchy node decorated with a direct vendor, aggregator vendors, a category and a sub-category. The declared response item schema instead describes user objects, which does not match the example payload.

nodes.label: PUT /master/material-assignments (Update Material Assignment)
nodes.rationale: There is no POST: assignment rows are materialised from the material hierarchy and only ever updated, which is why vendor_direct_id, category_id, sub_category_id and vendor_aggregator_ids are patched onto an existing id.

nodes.label: DELETE /master/material-assignments (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Marked deprecated:true and its request body is an exact copy of the update payload; deletion is superseded by the is_active flag on the update operation.

edges.source_location: put/get on the same path item
delete request body is an exact copy of the put request body
rows carry parent_id, server_groups and group_type extended_material_group, mirroring the material hierarchy record
category_id and sub_category_id reference master categories
vendor_direct_id and vendor_aggregator_ids reference master vendors
declared 200 response item schema describes user objects (id, name, email, username, type) while the example returns assignment rows; likely a copy-paste artefact rather than a real relationship
both attach owners to a classification node so sourcing can be routed automatically: material assignments attach vendors, category matrices attach approval users
